column3: Create a multi-targeted (net10.0;net48) .NET console app in Visual Studio, edit Program.cs and the project file, then build and run against each target framework separately, capturing the console output.

column4: Trigger
Resolve the current user home directory.
Open Visual Studio.
Launch Visual Studio and wait for its main window.
column16: Visual Studio main window is open.

column4: Maximize the Visual Studio main window.
Find the Create a new project button.
Click Create a new project.

column3: Make sure language filter is set to all language
column4: Set language filter to All languages.

column3: Search for console app and next
column4: Locate the template search box.
Click into the search box.
Search for console app.
Locate the Console App template item.
Select the Console App template.
Click Next.
Click Next to go to Additional Information.
Notice the selected framework version and ensure the latest available version (.NET 10.0) is selected.
Find the Create button.
Click Create to generate the project.
Re-locate the VS window after project creation.
Maximize the VS window after creation.
Activate Visual Studio window.

column3: Make sure solution explorer is opened
column4: Open Solution Explorer.
Find the Solution Explorer tab.
Click Solution Explorer tab to bring the tree to front.
Locate the ConsoleApp project node and capture its name.

column3: Write the code at line 1 using System
column4: Write Program.cs with using System; directive to disk.
Validate using System; was written as the literal first line of Program.cs.
column16: using System; is the first line of Program.cs.

column4: Take screenshot of Program.cs write result.

column3: Double click project name in solution explorer
column4: Double-click the project node to open .csproj in the editor.
Write the multi-target .csproj file to disk.
Validate the .csproj file actually contains the multi-target TargetFrameworks.
Take screenshot of .csproj write result.

column3: Reload the project after the external TargetFrameworks edit
column4: Find the Reload projects warning banner button.
column16: A Reload projects warning banner appears.

column4: Click Reload projects to adopt the new multi-target csproj.
Build the solution (builds both net10.0 and net48).
column16: Solution builds for both net10.0 and net48.

column4: Take screenshot of the build result.
Run without debugging (Ctrl+F5).
Dismiss build error dialog if it appears.
Find the spawned debug console window.
Validate the run output actually reflects the net10.0 build output path.
Take screenshot of net10.0 console output.
Close the console window.

column3: Select net48 from the Debug Target framework dropdown
column4: Expand the Debug Target split-button dropdown next to the Run button.
Locate the Framework submenu entry.
Click the Framework submenu entry to expand it.
Locate the net48 framework item; fails the test if net48 is not offered.
column16: net48 is offered as a debug target framework.

column4: Select net48 as the debug target framework.
Run without debugging (Ctrl+F5).
Dismiss build error dialog if it appears.
Find the spawned debug console window.
Validate the run output actually reflects the net48 build output path.
Take screenshot of net48 console output.
Close the console window.
Close Visual Studio.
